clue.text: The presenter trod on a nasty mess

indicators.note: making a nasty mess of the words trod on a means jumbling their letters

explanation.surface: Someone at the front of the room stepped in something unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty mess' rearranges TRODONA, the letters of 'trod on a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A donator gives or presents something, so is literally one who presents a gift.

clue.text: To have done with disfigurement, took action about it

indicators.note: about means the action word surrounds the blemish word

parts.note: did means acted, took action
a scar is a disfigurement

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a damaged thing after acting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'it' is only a link. 'To have done with' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard is to throw away, to be finished with something.

clue.text: Puzzle — nothing more is needed!

parts.note: non is Latin for not, read here as nothing
plus means more, in addition

explanation.surface: A cry that no further crossword is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' is a verb here, not a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle or perplex them.

clue.text: A highly questionable account

parts.note: highly hints at height, so a story that is lofty in stature and hard to believe

explanation.surface: A dubious report.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated, unbelievable narrative is called by that name.

clue.text: Withdraw brochure after centre-spread appears

indicators.note: after puts the leaflet word behind the central letters
centre picks out the middle letters of the word spread

parts.note: a tract is a pamphlet or brochure

explanation.surface: A leaflet pulled once the middle pages are seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or recant.

clue.text: Call late with just cause

parts.note: late can mean former, which is ex
a claim is a rightful demand, a just cause for asking

explanation.surface: Ringing up late at night is excused by a good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out, to call out suddenly.

clue.text: New sort of lace — it's stretchy

indicators.note: a new sort of something is a remade version, so the letters of lace and it's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for a novel stretchy lace.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means springy, able to stretch and return.

clue.text: Caught with the money, have to act the fool

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
L stands for pound, the libra, a unit of money
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Someone nabbed with cash has to play the idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: To clown is to fool around, behaving comically.

clue.text: Big noise occupying a large dwelling

indicators.note: occupying means the noise word sits inside the other

parts.note: large means big, so a large is a big
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Loud sounds filling a big house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts DIN inside A BIG. 'Big noise' looks like a celebrity but is DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abiding is staying or remaining, in the old sense of dwelling somewhere.

clue.text: He controls many a horse with little hesitation

parts.note: M, Roman 1000, stands for many
a nag is a horse
er is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A trainer handles lots of horses with barely a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is someone in charge, who directs and runs things.

clue.text: Such clothing must fit one to a t

parts.note: one, a lone item, is single

explanation.surface: A garment should fit its wearer perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such clothing' leans on the cryptic reading: SINGLE (one) joined to T.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Kind of harp that's a wind instrument

definitions.text: Kind of harp that's a wind instrument

parts.words: Kind of harp that's a wind instrument
parts.note: a harp named after the Greek keeper of the winds, played by the breeze rather than by hand, so a stringed thing that is literally a wind instrument

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a harp being classed among wind instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aeolian harp is a box of strings sounded by moving air, named for Aeolus, god of winds.

clue.text: A man going to sea turning back to get a set of maps

indicators.note: turning back means the sailor word is read from right to left

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, a man going to sea

explanation.surface: A sailor heading out turns home to fetch his charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' reverses SALT (an old sailor) to TLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound book of maps.

clue.text: Coming to a sober conclusion

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who stays sober
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone reaches a clear-headed decision.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, a crossword staple for sober.
explanation.definitionFit: Attending a meeting means coming to it, being present there.

clue.text: Entertain the underworld boss with a drink

parts.note: Dis is the Roman ruler of the underworld
port is a fortified wine, a drink

explanation.surface: Host the king of Hades by offering him a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport is to amuse or divert, so to entertain oneself or others.

clue.text: The person ordering a great dish

explanation.surface: A diner commanding a huge platter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who charges gives orders or commands; a charger is also a large flat serving plate.

clue.text: Give credit for quality

explanation.surface: Acknowledging someone's merit.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute is to ascribe or credit; an attribute is a characteristic or trait.

clue.text: A painter flourishing in the old Syrian city?

parts.note: palmy means prosperous, flourishing
an RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist enjoying success in an ancient Middle Eastern town.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmyra is the ruined ancient caravan city in the Syrian desert.

clue.text: A Sicilian place — one part-devastated by a volcano

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters of one part are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A town in Sicily partly wrecked by Etna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' rearranges ONEPART. The town lies at the foot of Etna, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternò is a town in Sicily near Catania.

clue.text: Animals remain outside as ruled

indicators.note: outside means the stay word wraps round the cattle word

parts.note: to lie is to stay, remain
neat is an old word for cattle

explanation.surface: Beasts stay out in the open, as decreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal. NEAT is an old word for cattle, a crossword favourite for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineate means marked with lines, as ruled paper is.

clue.text: A good book about fruit supplying good nourishment

indicators.note: about means the book letters go round the fruit

parts.note: A plus NT, the New Testament, a good book
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A healthy-eating guide all about fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, wrapping 'A good book' (NT is the New Testament) round the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is food, sustenance.

clue.text: Exceptional need for basic furniture

explanation.surface: A remarkable shortage of something to put food on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part reads as 'no table': a lack of the most basic furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means remarkable or outstanding; split in two it reads as having no table, lacking basic furniture.

clue.text: Beastly food store? That depends!

parts.note: a container of feed for an animal, which depends in the sense of hanging from its face

explanation.surface: An animal's larder that is conditional.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of fodder hung on a horse's head is that feed container.

clue.text: Tear into bar to find an Irishman

indicators.note: into puts the tearing word inside the barring word

parts.note: to ban is to bar
to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: Rushing into a pub to find a man from Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal. 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb meaning to prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Brendan is an Irish man's name, after the saint.

clue.text: Strange-looking tree incorporated in design submitted

indicators.note: incorporated in means the jumbled tree goes inside the purpose word

parts.note: an end is a purpose or design

indicators.note: strange-looking means the letters of tree look odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd tree featured in a submitted plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange-looking' signals the anagram and 'incorporated in' the container; design in the sense of aim or purpose is easily missed.
explanation.definitionFit: Entered means put in, as an entry submitted for a competition.

clue.text: Skin-treatment is their business

parts.note: skin here is animal hide, and the treatment is curing it into leather in a works devoted to that trade

explanation.surface: Sounds like beauty salons offering facials.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where hides are cured into leather are the workplaces this trade runs.

clue.text: Cream — some people feel it endangers health

indicators.note: some means only part of the words feel it endangers is used

explanation.surface: Some think cream is bad for you.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, the elite.

clue.text: Not at all appropriate in English exercise

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Something unsuitable turns up in a school language lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means unsuitable, out of place, or clumsy.

clue.text: To feel strongly about a lie's unusual

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of a lie's are set out in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone is moved by how strange a falsehood is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ALIES (from 'a lie's') to ALISE, after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to grasp it vividly, to be keenly aware of it.

clue.text: The knave restrained by the monarch

parts.note: bound means tied up, restrained
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A rogue held captive by the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounder is a cad, a dishonourable man, much as a knave is.

clue.text: Gorge all through tea maybe

parts.note: over can mean throughout, as in all over

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of tea could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Stuffing oneself the whole way through afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself, to eat too much.

clue.text: Picked up key and tipped

parts.note: G is a musical key
leaned means tipped or tilted

explanation.surface: Someone collected a key and gave a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit, so gleaned means collected or learned.
